title: Letter and Uniform
premise: In 1911, on a pearl-fishing coast where the trading company owns every debt and every name in its ledger, Marguerite Sandoval has survived by being useful and unremarkable. When the colonial army requisitions the town for war against the neighboring archipelago, they seize the company ledger—recording who owes what, who is native-born, and who once signed friendship papers with islanders now declared enemy. Marguerite's own name sits beside a promise she made as a child to an island boy, Tomas, who saved her from drowning: that she would warn his family if ships ever came for them. As the army uses the ledger to round up 'enemy sympathizers,' Marguerite must choose between the invisibility that kept her alive and the debt of a promise, smuggling Tomas's family toward open water while the officer who holds the ledger begins matching names to faces. The book ends with Marguerite surrendering her own page from the ledger to buy the family's escape, accepting indenture to the army itself so that others go free—and keeping, at last, one true name of her own.
about_author: E. M. Voss is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial shipping ledgers before turning to fiction. Their work explores how ordinary people are recorded, erased, and remembered by institutions.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A day in the oyster beds establishes her world: the company store, her mother's drowned lungs, the arithmetic of debt. She recalls, briefly, a boy named Tomas who pulled her from the sea ten years ago. Emotional beat: quiet endurance, the comfort of routine about to break.

chapters.title: Ledger Days
chapters.summary: Marguerite works in the company office copying accounts, where she sees every family's name reduced to figures—including her own indenture papers. The clerk warns her never to touch the original books. Emotional beat: the seduction and danger of knowing too much; she learns power lives in paper.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV, visiting secretly by night. He brings word that war is coming and asks Marguerite to remember her childhood promise. She deflects, afraid. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing; the past refusing to stay buried beneath practical survival.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Army gunboats anchor in the harbor; officers requisition the town, the warehouses, and—the clerk's horror—the company ledgers. Marguerite watches her name carried off in a crate. Emotional beat: dread; the machinery of belonging and ownership changing hands.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Reads
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Harrow's POV. He begins cross-referencing the ledger against census rolls to identify enemy sympathizers, finding the entry: Sandoval, M.—witness to islander rescue, bond sworn. He finds it curious rather than damning—for now. Emotional beat: cold intellectual menace; a hunter who enjoys his work.

chapters.title: Busy Hands
chapters.summary: Marguerite volunteers for laundry and mending duty at the garrison to stay close to the records room. She maps guard rotations in her head and passes warnings through the fishwives' gossip network. Emotional beat: purpose hardening into resolve; invisibility weaponized.

chapters.title: What the Pearl Remembers
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, alternating young Marguerite and young Tomas. The drowning, the rescue, the oath sworn over a broken pearl shell. Emotional beat: tenderness and weight; readers finally see exactly what was promised, and by whom.

chapters.title: Names Called at Dawn
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The first arrests: families with island kin are taken to the stockade. A neighbor she warned is among them because she moved too slowly. Emotional beat: grief and self-recrimination; the price of caution measured in other people's freedom.

chapters.title: A Debt in Ink
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. His family hides in the mangroves; his father refuses to flee without the deed-papers proving their fishing rights, which are locked in the requisitioned warehouse. Emotional beat: pride versus survival; Tomas realizes he must ask Marguerite for more than warning.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Confession
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The old clerk, dying and ashamed, tells her the ledger can be altered—but only by someone with access and a steady hand—and gives her his key. Emotional beat: an inheritance of complicity; the passing of moral burden from one generation to another.

chapters.title: Harrow's Dinner Table
chapters.summary: Harrow's POV. At dinner with the company factor, Harrow reveals he knows about the sworn bond and suspects the rescuer still lives nearby. He lets slip that the islanders' camp will be swept within the week. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Forging Tides
chapters.summary: Marguerite alters the ledger by lamplight, striking sympathetic names and forging travel permits. Her hands shake; she nearly destroys everything when Harrow almost catches her. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration; she crosses from witness to conspirator.

chapters.title: The Fishwife's Net
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, Marguerite's POV. The town's women coordinate the escape plan hidden inside a legitimate cargo run: Tomas's family concealed in the hold of a drying-boat. Emotional beat: solidarity; the invisible network becoming visible to itself.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Salt Market
chapters.summary: A paid informer tips Harrow; two helpers are arrested, and the boat is impounded. Marguerite watches from the crowd, unrecognized but marked. Emotional beat: despair and fury; the cost of the plan rising faster than its chances.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Harrow's POV. He questions the arrested fishwife gently, patiently, peeling back the network thread by thread. Marguerite's name surfaces—but so does evidence of the clerk's alterations, muddying the trail. Emotional beat: mounting dread; suspicion narrowing like a noose.

chapters.title: The Last Permit
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With days left, she forges one final set of papers and decides the boat cannot wait for the deed-papers after all. She confronts Tomas: run now or lose everyone. Emotional beat: fierce clarity; love expressed as ultimatum.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The escape launch departs into a building squall; Harrow's patrol boat gives chase. Tomas's father throws the deed-papers overboard to lighten the boat—a symbolic release of the past. Emotional beat: sacrifice and liberation entangled.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Climax, Marguerite's POV. Harrow corners her in the records room with the forged pages spread between them. Instead of denying it, she claims sole authorship, protecting the network, and offers him the thing he truly wants: her confession, complete and signed. Emotional beat: courage at full price; she stops hiding.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Harrow's POV. Facing transfer and scandal if the altered ledger becomes public, Harrow accepts her bargain: her voluntary indenture to the army labor corps in exchange for dropping the investigation. Emotional beat: ambiguous victory; justice bent, not broken.

chapters.title: Departures
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Word arrives that Tomas's family reached neutral water. She says goodbye to the town, the beds, her mother's grave, boarding the transport north. Emotional beat: bittersweet farewell; survival achieved, home surrendered.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, months later in the labor corps. She writes letters for illiterate workers, quietly restoring names the army reduced to numbers. Among them she signs her first letter simply 'Marguerite'—no company mark, no debt attached. Emotional beat: reclamation; identity rebuilt from service.

chapters.title: Letter and Uniform
chapters.summary: Final chapter, split POV. Years later, peace declared, Tomas returns and finds Marguerite released, running a small letter-writing stall by the harbor. Between them lies not the old oath but a new choice, freely made. Emotional beat: resolution and hope; memory honored, belonging chosen rather than assigned.
